Top Hip Bursitis Treatments in Hyderabad: Expert Guide

Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy25 February 2026

Introduction

Living with hip pain can be challenging, especially when everyday activities become difficult. One of the common causes of hip pain is hip bursitis, a condition that affects the fluid-filled sacs, known as bursae, which cushion the areas where muscles and tendons glide over bones. Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy, a renowned Senior Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon at Apollo Hospitals, Financial District, Hyderabad, provides expert diagnosis and treatment for hip bursitis to help patients regain mobility and live pain-free.

What is Hip Bursitis?

Hip bursitis refers to the inflammation of the bursae located around the hip joint. The condition results in pain and discomfort, particularly on the outside of the hip. Those living in Hyderabad and dealing with hip pain might find relief at Apollo Hospitals, where Dr. Harsha offers specialized care.

Symptoms and Causes of Hip Bursitis

  • Persistent hip pain, especially when lying on the affected side.
  • Swelling and tenderness around the hip area.
  • Pain that increases with prolonged activity.
  • Stiffness or reduced range of motion in the hip.

Hip bursitis can be triggered by repetitive friction, direct trauma, or pressure on the bursae. Other contributing factors may include arthritis, leg-length discrepancies, or infections.

Treatment Options

If you are experiencing symptoms of hip bursitis, a variety of treatment options are available to alleviate pain and restore function. At Apollo Hospitals, Financial District, Hyderabad, Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy tailors treatment plans to meet individual patient needs.

Conservative treatments such as rest, ice application, and anti-inflammatory medications can often manage mild cases of hip bursitis. Physical therapy is also beneficial for strengthening surrounding muscles and improving joint mobility. For persistent or severe cases, corticosteroid injections may be administered directly into the inflamed bursae to reduce inflammation and pain.

In rare instances, when conservative measures fail, surgery may be necessary to remove the affected bursa. Dr. Harsha, with his extensive experience, utilizes minimally invasive surgical techniques to ensure rapid recovery and minimal discomfort for the patient.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How is hip bursitis diagnosed?

A: Hip bursitis is typically diagnosed through a combination of a physical examination, patient history, and imaging tests such as X-rays or MRI to rule out other conditions.

Q: Can hip bursitis heal on its own?

A: Mild cases of hip bursitis can improve with self-care and conservative treatments. However, if symptoms persist, it is advisable to seek professional medical attention to prevent further complications.

Q: What lifestyle changes can help manage hip bursitis?

A: Maintaining a healthy weight, engaging in low-impact exercises, and using proper techniques during physical activities can help manage and prevent hip bursitis.
